message.content:
{
  "screen_decision": "include",
  "screen_rationale": "The study reports quantitative measures of agreement between zebrafish model results and human clinical outcomes, specifically sensitivity (68%), specificity (89%), and accuracy (78%) for predicting drug toxicity. It uses whole zebrafish larvae as the in vivo model.",
  "arm": "toxicology",
  "arm_evidence": "We will show that by using ZeGlobaltox, a high toxicity predictivity is achieved—specificity (89%), sensitivity (68%), and accuracy (78%).",
  "therapeutic_areas": [
    "hepatic",
    "cardiovascular",
    "neurology-stroke",
    "cross-cutting"
  ],
  "areas_evidence": "Thus, the proposed approach allows the independent analysis of cardio-, neuro-, and hepatotoxicity effects in the same animal",
  "model_type": "across-multiple-models",
  "model_evidence": "The ZeGlobalTox assay has been designed as a medium-throughput platform to detect, in the same animal, the three most concerning toxicities causing drug attrition, namely cardio-, neuro-, and hepatotoxicity.",
  "species": [
    "zebrafish"
  ],
  "species_evidence": "Based on these facts, we have developed the ZeGlobalTox assay, an innovative experimental procedure that addresses organ-specific toxicity of different drugs on zebrafish larvae (up to 5 dpf).",
  "endpoint_class": "mixed",
  "endpoint_evidence": "Four cardiac parameters were evaluated to assess whether a compound was cardiotoxic: heart rate (beats per minute, BPM), QTc prolongation, ejection fraction (EJF), and cardiac arrest. ... Decreased motility was detected in MPTP, paracetamol, and trifluoperazine-HCL treated larvae ... Three phenotypic endpoints were analysed for hepatotoxicity evaluation: liver area, steatosis, and yolk lipid retention."
}
